transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because once I start worrying about something, I can’t seem to put it aside. It might be my mother getting up at night, a grant report, or whether I missed something at work. I make lists and try to redirect myself, but it just keeps coming back.
How long have you been experiencing this persistent worrying?
It’s been about a year and two months. It really started after my mother moved into my home following her fall.
Alongside this worry, have you also been feeling down, sad, or depressed most of the time?
I’m not really sure. I’ve been so focused on the worrying that I haven’t thought of it as feeling depressed.
Do you find yourself repeating certain actions or mental routines over and over, such as checking things repeatedly, to try to relieve your worry?
I don’t think I do anything like that repeatedly. I mean, I try to make lists or distract myself, but not in a ritual kind of way.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you normally enjoy doing?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really paid attention to that—I’ve mostly just been focused on everything I need to worry about.
Have you noticed any physical tension in your body, like tight muscles or aches, along with the constant worrying?

Yes. By the end of the day, my neck and shoulders feel really locked up, like I’ve been bracing myself all day. I also catch myself clenching my jaw, especially when I’m answering emails or listening for my mother in the next room.
Have you had any trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or feeling rested in the morning?

Most nights I have trouble falling asleep because I’m replaying the day and trying to plan for every possible problem. And if I wake up hearing my mother moving around, I can be awake for an hour or two afterward. By the time I get to the library, it feels like I never really rested.

inference_history.note: Initial presentation of pervasive, difficult-to-control worry across multiple domains (family, work) raises concern primarily for generalized anxiety disorder, with obsessive-compulsive disorder, adjustment disorder, and mood/anxiety spectrum disorders as differentials.
Duration of 14 months with generalized worry across multiple domains makes Adjustment Disorder (F43.2) unlikely, so it has been ruled out.
